Trail Physics · Unit 1: Physics Foundations · Module 3

Scientific Measurement

SI units, conversions, scientific notation, significant figures and uncertainty: how to collect data and say how sure you are.

Lesson coming

The question

Your GPS says 38 km/h. A timing gate says 35. Which one do you trust?

The physics

  • SI and derived units
  • Unit conversion
  • Scientific notation
  • Significant figures
  • Uncertainty
  • Estimation
  • Models and assumptions

The math

  • 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h
  • percent uncertainty = (uncertainty ÷ measured value) × 100%

Learning objectives

  • Use SI base and derived units
  • Convert between units, such as km/h, m/s and mph
  • Write and calculate with scientific notation
  • Report a result with sensible significant figures
  • Estimate a measurement’s uncertainty and percent uncertainty
  • Name a model’s assumptions and when they stop holding

The mountain biking connection

Riders measure everything: jump heights, split times, slope grade, suspension sag. Every measurement has an uncertainty, and different tools have different precision.
